name: Attio

identity.note: Attio is the AI-native CRM (attio.com); not to be confused with other products with similar names.

summary: Attio is a customizable CRM platform with a public REST API, webhooks, an app SDK and a hosted MCP server.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow (optionally PKCE, workspace- or user-level tokens) for multi-workspace apps; workspace admin-generated access token (API key) with scopes for a single workspace. Tokens are sent as Bearer.

gates: Workspace API keys can only be created by workspace admins; available on all plans
Unpublished OAuth apps can be installed in at most 25 workspaces; publishing needs an approved release
Workspace-level OAuth tokens can only be granted by workspace admins; a non-admin member's install request needs admin approval

api.note: The OpenAPI spec is public at api.attio.com/openapi/api. There are documented rate limits, cursor pagination, and OAuth scopes per endpoint. The page also lists an App SDK and a SQL surface.

mcp.note: Hosted by Attio and documented at docs.attio.com/mcp/overview. It uses OAuth as the user, with read operations auto-approved and write operations asking for confirmation. It covers records, activities, notes, tasks and meetings.

open_questions: Does a free Attio workspace plan give full API access? The help page says API keys are on all plans, but I did not check plan pages for other limits.
The exact rate-limit numbers were not fetched.
The marketplace review criteria for publishing a public OAuth app were not read in detail.

claims.text: There are two ways to get tokens: OAuth 2.0 and a workspace API key. OAuth is preferred for multi-workspace apps.
claims.quote: You should prefer the OAuth 2.0 flow if building an app for multiple workspaces. If you are building an app for a single workspace, you can manually generate an API key

claims.text: API keys are available on all plans, and only admins can create them.
claims.quote: Available on all plans.

claims.text: An unpublished OAuth app can be installed in up to 25 workspaces.
claims.quote: An unpublished app can be installed in up to 25 workspaces.

claims.text: Attio exposes a public REST API with a public OpenAPI specification.
claims.quote: Attio provides a public REST API which exchanges JSON over HTTPS.

claims.text: Attio hosts its own official MCP server, with OAuth sign-in.
claims.quote: Attio MCP is Attio’s hosted MCP server that gives AI tools secure access to your Attio workspace.

name: HubSpot

identity.note: HubSpot CRM and Hubs (Marketing, Sales, Service, Content, Operations, Commerce). Date-based API versioning (e.g. 2026-03, 2026-09) alongside legacy v1-v4 endpoints.

summary: HubSpot is a CRM and customer platform covering marketing, sales, service, content and operations, with a broad public API and an official hosted MCP server.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0 is required for apps used across multiple accounts (distribution 'marketplace' or 'private', private capped at 10 accounts). Static auth access tokens, found in app settings, are for a single account. Client-credentials tokens are used only for webhooks journal. The remote MCP server uses OAuth with PKCE via an MCP connector created in HubSpot.

gates: OAuth apps distributed to many accounts must use distribution 'marketplace' (listing on the HubSpot Marketplace) or 'private' (allowlisted accounts, max 10 installed at a time).
Test installs use free developer test accounts; installing an unverified app requires ticking an authorization checkbox.

Some endpoints and MCP tools depend on the customer's subscription tier (e.g. Quotes need Revenue Hub Pro/Enterprise, AEO needs Marketing Hub Pro/Enterprise, custom pipelines unavailable on free tools).
Installing users need the required HubSpot user permissions; MCP actions respect those user permissions.

api.note: Base URL is https://api.hubapi.com. Date-based versioning (e.g. /crm/objects/2026-09/contacts); older versions keep working until their end-of-life date. Rate limits were not checked.

mcp.note: HubSpot hosts a remote MCP server for reading and writing CRM records and more. It uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE through an MCP connector created in HubSpot (Development > MCP Connectors). HubSpot also ships a local Developer MCP server for building apps.

blocker: Distributing an OAuth app to many customers needs HubSpot Marketplace listing (distribution 'marketplace'), or is limited to 10 allowlisted accounts. Some endpoints depend on the customer's HubSpot subscription tier.
open_questions: Is a free developer account sufficient to create apps? The sources fetched covered test accounts, not account signup.
Exact rate limits were not verified.
Marketplace review requirements were not fetched.
Per-endpoint plan gating (which APIs need paid tiers) was not enumerated.

claims.text: OAuth is required for apps distributed to multiple accounts; static auth tokens are for a single account.
claims.quote: OAuth is required for multiple accounts, while static auth access tokens are used for installing in a single account at a time.

claims.text: Private distribution caps installs at 10 accounts, while marketplace distribution makes the app eligible for Marketplace listing.
claims.quote: If you choose this option, you can install your app in a maximum of 10 accounts at a time.

claims.text: Developers can test in developer test accounts, which they create themselves in HubSpot.
claims.quote: click **Create developer test account**. Follow the prompts to create your new test account.

claims.text: The REST API lives at api.hubapi.com with date-based versioning, and older versions keep working until their end-of-life date.
claims.quote: All APIs, whether legacy, new, or beta, use the same root path as before: `https://api.hubapi.com/`.

claims.text: HubSpot publishes a hosted remote MCP server that reads and writes CRM records.
claims.quote: The remote HubSpot MCP server is a publicly hosted endpoint for connecting external AI tools and applications to HubSpot’s CRM.

claims.text: The MCP server requires OAuth with PKCE through a connector created in a HubSpot account.
claims.quote: PKCE is required for authenticating with HubSpot’s MCP server.

claims.text: Some MCP tools depend on the customer's subscription tier.
claims.quote: is available in HubSpot accounts with a *Revenue Hub Professional* or *Enterprise* subscription.

name: Close

identity.note: Close (close.com) is the sales CRM, not other products named Close.

summary: Close is a sales CRM for managing leads, contacts, opportunities, calls, emails, SMS and tasks.

auth.detail: API keys created in Settings > Developer > API Keys, sent via HTTP Basic (key as username, empty password). OAuth 2.0 apps created in Close; private by default, public needs Close approval.

gates: OAuth apps are Private by default (only your own Close organization can authorize them); making one public for other customers requires requesting publication from Close
All OAuth apps get all.full_access offline_access scopes only
Close itself is a paid SaaS (trial availability and API plan-gating not verified on pricing pages)

api.note: REST at https://api.close.com/api/v1; rate limits with 429 backoff; experimental OpenAPI spec at api.close.com/api/openapi.json (incomplete coverage); event log covers last 30 days.

mcp.note: Vendor-hosted remote MCP (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 DCR, or API key header) with scopes mcp.read, mcp.write_safe, mcp.write_destructive.

blocker: Public multi-customer OAuth distribution requires Close to approve making the OAuth app public. API key auth works per customer without review. Whether a trial or plan tier is needed for API access was not verified.
open_questions: Is API access available on all Close plans and on the free trial?
What is the review process and timeline for making an OAuth app public (developer.close.com/integrations/publish)?
What are the exact rate limits?

claims.text: API keys are created in account settings and used with HTTP Basic auth.
claims.quote: API keys can be created and managed in your Close account under **Settings** → **Developer** → **API Keys**.

claims.text: Both API keys and OAuth 2.0 are supported.
claims.quote: All API requests require authentication. Two methods are supported:

claims.text: OAuth apps are created in a Close account with a client ID and secret, with full access scopes only.

claims.text: REST API with JSON, webhooks, an event log and an experimental OpenAPI spec.
claims.quote: Close uses industry-standard REST conventions with predictable URL structures, standard HTTP methods, and JSON request/response bodies.

name: SE Ranking

identity.note: Covers the Data API, Project API, Local Marketing API and SE Visible API. One API key works for both the Data API and the Project API.

summary: SE Ranking is an all-in-one SEO platform for rank tracking, keyword research, backlinks, site audits and AI search visibility, and it exposes REST APIs and a hosted MCP server.

auth.detail: Users generate an API key in the API Dashboard. It is sent as 'Authorization: Token KEY' or as an apikey query parameter. One key covers the Data API and Project API. The hosted MCP server also supports OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, but the REST API has no third-party OAuth app model.

gates: Data API requests use API credits. Every current paid plan includes a monthly allowance, from 10,000 on Essential to 100,000 on Business, Growth and Enterprise.
More credits cost extra: pay-as-you-go packs from $50 for 250,000 credits, an API add-on from $540 per year, or a standalone API plan from $2,148 per year.
The Project API draws on subscription limits such as projects, keywords and audits.
Sub-accounts cannot use API access directly. The master account's key is needed until sub-account keys are released.
A free trial reportedly includes 100K API credits. This comes from search snippets only, not a fetched page.

api.note: Base URL is https://api.seranking.com. Only successful 2xx responses consume credits, and each endpoint has per-request and per-record credit costs. Webhooks are listed only because 'other' was needed to cover the Postman collection. I did not confirm that webhooks exist.

mcp.note: The vendor hosts a remote MCP server over Streamable HTTP. It supports OAuth 2.1 or an X-Api-Key header and is listed as an official connector for Claude and ChatGPT. The vendor also has a GitHub repo, seranking/seo-data-api-mcp-server. Not every API endpoint is exposed through MCP.

blocker: The user needs a paid SE Ranking plan, or a trial, to get an API key. Data API usage is metered in credits, and a sub-account needs the master account's key.
open_questions: The free trial and its 100K credits came from search snippets only. I did not fetch the sign-up or pricing page to confirm them.
Exact rate limits were not checked.
Whether Project API access is available on trial accounts was not confirmed.

claims.quote: A single API key authenticates every endpoint across the Data API and the Project API.

claims.text: The key is sent in the Authorization header with the Token scheme, or as an apikey query parameter.
claims.quote: Include an `Authorization` header in your request, with the value `Token YOUR_API_KEY`.

claims.quote: All Essential, Pro, Business, Core, Growth, and Enterprise plans include Data API access with a monthly credit allowance:

claims.quote: The Project API is available on every current subscription plan: Essential, Pro, Business, Core, Growth, and Enterprise.

name: Mermaid CLI

identity.note: Local open-source CLI (@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli) for the Mermaid diagram library. Distinct from the hosted Mermaid Chart / mermaid.ai product, which has its own account, API and official MCP server.

summary: Command-line tool and Node.js library that renders Mermaid diagram definitions (or Mermaid code blocks in Markdown) to SVG, PNG or PDF using headless Chromium via Puppeteer.

auth.detail: No remote service or credentials. It is an MIT-licensed npm package, Docker image or local binary that runs on the user's machine.

gates: Local tool only: it needs Node.js and a headless Chromium (Puppeteer) install, or the Docker image.
Running in containers or as root on Linux can hit sandbox issues that need a puppeteer config workaround.
Not a hosted API, so Composio would need a sandbox or local execution runtime to run it.

api.note: CLI `mmdc` with options for theme, background, size, CSS file, icon packs and puppeteer config. Node API `run(input, output, options)`. Docker images are minlag/mermaid-cli and ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli. Rendering needs a browser.

mcp.note: mermaid-js does not publish an MCP server for mermaid-cli. Third-party servers wrap it, such as andrewginns/mermaid-mcp-server (Python, calls npx @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli) and peng-shawn/mermaid-mcp-server. The Mermaid Chart company runs a separate official hosted MCP at mcp.mermaid.ai, but it belongs to the commercial Mermaid Chart product, not this CLI.

blocker: It is a local CLI and library with no remote API or auth. It has a narrow scope (render diagrams) and needs Node and headless Chromium at runtime, so it only works as a local or sandboxed tool, not as a normal cloud-API toolkit.
open_questions: Does Composio want local-execution or sandbox toolkits? If so, this could be wrapped as a render_diagram tool.
Would the hosted Mermaid Chart (mermaid.ai) API or its official MCP be the better target? It was not assessed in depth.

claims.text: mermaid-cli is a CLI that converts Mermaid definitions to SVG/PNG/PDF, with basic Markdown support.
claims.quote: It takes a mermaid definition file as input and generates an SVG/PNG/PDF file as output. There's basic support for converting mermaid code blocks embedded within Markdown files.

claims.text: It is installed locally from npm and run offline with the mmdc command; no credentials are involved.
claims.quote: npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli

claims.text: It is distributed as an MIT-licensed public repository, and Docker images are also provided, so developers need no signup.
claims.quote: docker pull ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli

claims.text: It also exposes a Node.js programmatic API via a run function.
claims.quote: import { run } from "@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli";

claims.text: A third-party MCP server wraps mermaid-cli by calling it as a subprocess.
claims.quote: The server internally calls `npx @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` as a subprocess to perform diagram validation and rendering.

name: PitchBook

identity.note: PitchBook (a Morningstar company). Research/data API (api.pitchbook.com) is a separate paid product (Direct Data); docs are in a Postman collection.

summary: PitchBook is a private and public capital markets intelligence provider with data on companies, investors, funds, deals, and people, exposed via a licensed REST API and a vendor-hosted MCP.

auth.detail: Static API key issued by PitchBook after contract, sent as 'Authorization: PB-Token {API_KEY}'. No OAuth for the REST API. Calls also consume purchased API credits. The Premium MCP server reportedly uses OAuth (third-party listings only).

gates: API is a separate offering from the PitchBook Platform requiring a standalone contract agreement
Sandbox key must be requested from account manager
API credits must be purchased; each call has a cost (402 if insufficient)
Endpoint access depends on what is licensed in the contract
No self-serve signup; request goes through the Direct Data team
PitchBook Data MCP is live but only available to customers upon request

api.note: Base URL https://api.pitchbook.com. Credit-based per-call pricing, rate limits (429) and per-endpoint permissions (403). No public SDKs found. Docs only in a Postman collection.

mcp.note: Vendor-hosted PitchBook Premium MCP / PitchBook Data MCP, covering company, deal, investor and fund data. The press release says Data MCP is available to customers upon request. The URL and OAuth come from third-party listings, not vendor pages I fetched.

blocker: No self-serve access. The API needs a standalone contract with PitchBook's Direct Data team, and a sandbox key comes via an account manager. API credits must also be purchased.
open_questions: Are API rate limits and credit prices published anywhere? Not found.
Does the Premium MCP (premium.mcp.pitchbook.com) use OAuth that a third-party platform like Composio can register for, or is it limited to approved partners?
Is there a partner or reseller program that gives Composio shared credentials?
